title: BiNeuroRAM: Energy-Efficient ReRAM-Based PIM for Accurate Bipolar Spiking Neural Network Acceleration
problem: Existing ReRAM-based neuromorphic accelerators suffer from high sensing power and accuracy degradation when running spiking neural networks, limiting their deployment.
motivation: SNNs offer energy efficiency through event-driven processing, but ReRAM sensing overhead and neuron model limitations prevent competitive accuracy on standard benchmarks.
method: BiNeuroRAM uses ReRAM-based processing-in-memory with three innovations: (1) support for spike-tracing bipolar-integrate-and-fire (ST-BIF) neurons enabling higher accuracy; (2) low-power voltage sense amplifier (LPVSA) reducing ReRAM read power by 14.7-58.2x via optimized sensing; (3) asynchronous micro-architecture exploiting event-driven SNN sparsity to maximize throughput.
key_novelty: First ReRAM accelerator supporting ST-BIF neurons while reducing sensing power by orders of magnitude through specialized LPVSA design.
contributions: Achieves 80.9% ImageNet accuracy with ResNet-18 SNNs, 8.4% higher than prior SNN accelerators
Introduces LPVSA reducing ReRAM read power by 14.7-58.2x
Demonstrates 2.08x throughput and 2.09x energy efficiency vs. IF-based SNN accelerators
limitations: Not discussed in abstract; likely focuses on ImageNet but scalability to other modalities unclear.
primary_theme: ReRAM-based neuromorphic computing with advanced neuron models
